name: Public cord-blood-unit banking: controlled-rate freezing in 10% DMSO and long-term storage in the liquid phase of liquid nitrogen at -196 C
plain_name: Bank umbilical cord blood for transplants in liquid nitrogen
description: Red-cell- and plasma-depleted cord blood units with DMSO/dextran cryoprotectant are frozen at a controlled rate and stored (up to 19 years) immersed in liquid nitrogen at -196 C, well below the ~-130 C glass transition of water.
keywords: Bank umbilical cord blood for transplants in liquid nitrogen

sources.citation: Roh et al., Up to 19-year cryopreservation does not impair hematopoietic progenitor function in cord blood: a 1129-unit analysis from the largest Korean public cord blood bank, Stem Cells Transl Med. DOI 10.1093/stcltm/szag075

reported_equipment: liquid phase of liquid nitrogen storage (model not stated)

requirements.rationale: Units are stored immersed in the liquid phase of liquid nitrogen at -196 C.
Liquid-phase storage requires a vessel that holds liquid nitrogen.
Physical basis: below the ~-130 C glass transition of water biological activity stops; informative lower bound for any acceptable store.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
